name: Douhua
description: Silken tofu pudding set just barely and served in warm ginger syrup or sweet peanut broth as a gentle dessert.
ingredients: a handful of sliced scallion whites
a handful of fresh scallion greens, chopped
a generous spoonful of toasted sesame seeds
instructions: Preheat your oven (or set up your steamer or frying station) and lightly grease your pan or molds with toasted sesame oil.
In a large bowl, whisk together the steamed buns and star anise until evenly combined.
In a separate bowl, blend the soy sauce with the pork stock until smooth and well incorporated.
Gently fold the wet mixture into the dry ingredients, taking care not to overmix.
Transfer everything to your prepared pan or molds and cook — bake, steam, chill, or fry — until set, about 10 mins.
Remove from the heat and let it cool completely; this helps the texture firm up perfectly.
Garnish with cilantro or a dusting of toasted sesame seeds.
tips: Resist opening the oven door too early — a sudden change in temperature can cause the dessert to sink or crack.
This keeps well for a couple of days in an airtight container, and the flavor often improves overnight.
Bring your soy sauce to room temperature before mixing for a smoother, more even texture.
